hookLine: Thirty-four minutes past six, on a Saturday evening in Seoul, someone pushed their way out of a crowded alley

OP.secondary: A street about fifty metres long. Five metres wide at the top, three point two at the bottom.

ACT_1.secondary: About 50 metres long. Twenty-five seconds to walk, at a normal pace, without stopping.
Two cars side by side. The end that opens onto the main road.
A peer-reviewed reconstruction puts the average width of the alley at under four metres along its length.
An illegally extended terrace on the northern side — 17.2 square metres — along the side that faces the alley.
Foreign restaurants, bars that stay open, a few minutes from a station on two lines.
An estimated hundred thousand people, many in their teens and twenties, dressed in costume.
81,573 people left the train at Itaewon station that day.

ACT_1.primary: THE SAME SATURDAY, A YEAR EARLIER

ACT_1.secondary: A state-owned company was counting them as they came, hour by hour.

ACT_2.secondary: Police in Itaewon received eleven distress reports about dangerous levels of overcrowding.
In South Korea, the number you dial for the police.
People were being forced uphill into a place with no room to come back down. Somebody should come and control it.
One hour and thirty-five minutes after the first.
Two different calls. The same evening. The same street.
Long enough to drive across a country.
A report entering an organisation. What the organisation does with it is a separate question.
The room where the reports arrive.
None of the eleven describes an offence. They describe a street.
The calls exist as transcripts. That is why they can be counted at all.
This film does not claim that any single call, answered differently, would have changed the outcome.

ACT_3.secondary: Four researchers published a study of that night, reconstructing the crowd from the record.
The study records over three hundred people concentrated in that area. Eighteen square metres is a small bedroom.
Two directions, instead of every direction.
The study's timeline puts the first report of a crushing accident, involving approximately ten people, at this minute.
The police chief ordered all available personnel to the scene.
The first emergency rescue team arrived.
157 in the immediate aftermath. 158 by 14 November. 159 by 3 January.
Recorded by the ministry and carried by the reporting.
46 relatives of 21 of those 26 travelled to Seoul for a week, at the official invitation of the Korean government.
About one in ten may not have died of asphyxiation — crush syndrome, rhabdomyolysis, or organ damage from compression.

ACT_4.secondary: The number deployed in the district that night.
137 officers is not a token force.
Most of them working on crime rather than crowds.
It arrived on 23 October 2025 — three years later.
Rallies and demonstrations: 34 in the whole of 2021.

ACT_4.primary: THE OTHER PART OF THE DISTRICT
ACT_4.secondary: On the last Saturday in October, there were 137.

ACT_4.primary: WHAT THIS FILM DOES NOT SAY
ACT_4.secondary: That more officers would have changed the outcome. Nobody has established that.
A film that says would have about a hundred and fifty-nine deaths is making something up.
The National Assembly impeached the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
All nine judges of the Constitutional Court rejected the impeachment, unanimously. He was reinstated.

ACT_5.secondary: Former chief of the Yongsan police station. Sentenced at first instance to three years without labour.
Professional negligence resulting in death and injury.
Head of the station's 112 situation room. Two years without labour.
None of these convictions is final. Both appeals were later suspended by the court.
A hundred thousand people walking into a district because it is the twenty-ninth of October is not anybody's event.

ACT_5.primary: FRAMEWORK ACT ON THE MANAGEMENT OF DISASTERS AND SAFETY
ACT_5.secondary: Article 66-11: safety management measures when holding a local festival.
Held by somebody. That is what the article is for.
A member of the National Assembly proposed adding a penalty.
An administrative fine of up to two million won for failing to file a plan, and a power to demand a bad plan be improved.
The 13th criminal division of the Seoul High Court suspended the appeal of the former station chief and two officers from his 112 room.
A different bench did the same with the district office chief's appeal.
A criminal appeal about a hundred and fifty-nine deaths was paused by the court, because nobody had yet established what happened.
As this film is made, the appeals have not resumed.

ENDING.secondary: The city listed 71 areas where large crowds were expected, and put 909 cameras into them.

_readme: Every figure states something the narration states. The pairing is checkable: grep the
phrase in 06_audio/narration_index.v001.json and the chunk carrying it comes back.
TWO ARE LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE CUT.
ACT_4 'WHAT THIS FILM DOES NOT SAY' and "'WOULD HAVE'": the film states on screen that
nobody has established that more officers would have changed the outcome. Without them the
137-versus-100,000 cards read as an accusation the record does not support.
ACT_5 'APPEALS PENDING' and 'SUSPENDED, NOT DECIDED': Lee Im-jae, Song Byung-ju and the
district office chief are living men whose appeals are SUSPENDED. Every card naming a
conviction is followed by a card saying it is not final. R3 depends on that pairing.
